title: 7 new dementia risk factors revealed — including one millions struggle with
summary: The World Health Organization has added seven new dementia risk factors, including stroke, sleep apnea, HIV and air pollution, to its updated guidelines.
story: Psychiatrist Daniel Amen discusses updated global recommendations for reducing cognitive decline, highlighting hormones, cardiovascular health, restorative rest, sensory loss, social connection and other factors tied to healthy aging.
The World Health Organization (WHO) has released a major update to its guidelines on reducing the risk of cognitive decline and dementia.
The second edition of the original 2019 report was updated to "reflect the latest evidence and advances in dementia risk reduction."
The following seven additional health conditions and exposures were added to the list.
LEARNING ANOTHER LANGUAGE MAY KEEP YOUR BRAIN YOUNGER, STUDY SUGGESTS
Stroke
Traumatic brain injury
Vision impairment
Sleep problems
HIV
Air pollution
Menopausal hormone therapy
The WHO's updated guidelines "reflect the latest evidence and advances in dementia risk reduction." (iStock)
These new risk factors joined the previously existing 12, which are listed below.
Cognitive activity
Social activity
Physical inactivity
Harmful alcohol use
Tobacco use
Unhealthy diet/nutrition
Obesity
Diabetes
Hypertension
Dyslipidemia (abnormal amount of lipids (fats) or lipoproteins in the blood)
Hearing loss
Depression
WARDING OFF ALZHEIMER'S MIGHT MEAN MAKING THESE 11 LIFESTYLE CHANGES, EXPERT SAYS
Dr. Daniel Amen, physician and founder of Amen Clinics in California, has his own formula for reducing Alzheimer’s risk factors, following an acronym called BRIGHT MINDS.

This stands for blood flow, retirement and aging, inflammation, genetics, head trauma, toxins, mental health, immunity and infections, neurohormones, diabesity (co-occurrence of obesity and type 2 diabetes) and sleep. The WHO’s updated guidelines offer similar advice.
Menopausal hormone therapy is primarily used to treat symptoms of menopause. (iStock)
Amen spoke with Fox News Digital about the new additions to the WHO's list of risk factors.
Menopausal hormone therapy (MHT)

The WHO does not recommend menopausal hormone therapy specifically to prevent dementia in postmenopausal women 65 and older. For younger women, it says there is not enough evidence to determine whether MHT affects dementia risk.

Amen agreed that there is not enough evidence to support using MHT specifically to prevent dementia. He said hormonal changes during menopause may affect mood and memory, although the relationship between MHT and dementia risk remains uncertain.
'I'M A NEUROLOGIST — HERE'S WHY DEMENTIA IS RISING AND HOW TO REDUCE YOUR RISK’

"For women, as they go through menopause, lower progesterone makes them anxious, and [with] lower estrogen, they start to have memory problems," he said. "Hormone replacement early on is helpful, and that's what we see on the brain imaging work that we do."
Experts note that while menopause-related hormonal changes can be associated with mood and cognitive symptoms, these effects can vary widely.
Stroke
A stroke occurs when blood flow to part of the brain is blocked or when a blood vessel in or near the brain bursts, according to the American Stroke Association.
Conditions that affect the heart and blood vessels can also affect brain health and are associated with a higher risk of dementia, according to Amen.
Any blood flow blockages can impact brain health and increase the risk of dementia. (iStock)
That can include conditions such as heart disease, heart rhythm problems, stroke and transient ischemic attacks. Erectile dysfunction can also be associated with underlying vascular disease, he said.
"And 40% of 40-year-olds have erectile dysfunction, 70% of 70-year-olds. So, if I'm an older person, I'm thinking if I get my brain right, my love life could be better, too," Amen added.
Traumatic brain injury (TBI)
Amen surmised that the WHO is "late to the party" in emphasizing the importance of head trauma as a dementia risk factor. TBI can range from a mild concussion to a severe brain injury.
COMMON VACCINE LINKED TO 24% LOWER DEMENTIA RISK IN OLDER ADULTS

"One of the big lessons from the brain imaging work we do is that mild traumatic brain injury ruins people's lives," he said. "They end up seeing psychiatrists because they have temper problems or ... depression or anxiety, and it's really from a snowmobiling accident in [their] 30s."
Amen added that failing to protect the brain — which he described as "very soft" and having the consistency of "soft butter" — is "not the smart thing to do."
"Mild traumatic brain injury ruins people's lives," the brain expert said. (iStock)
Vision impairment
A significant portion of the brain is dedicated to vision, according to Amen.
"So, if your vision becomes troubled, your brain's troubled," he said.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Amen said vision impairment may place additional demands on the brain. While the condition has been linked with cognitive decline, the WHO says there is insufficient evidence to recommend vision treatment specifically for dementia prevention.
Sleep disorders
Sleep appears to support the brain’s waste-clearance processes, Amen noted.
Sleep challenges affect tens of millions of Americans. In 2024, 30.5% of U.S. adults reported getting less than seven hours of shut-eye per day, according to the CDC.
For those with sleep problems such as sleep apnea, it can cause changes in the brain that resemble the hallmarks of Alzheimer’s disease, the expert said.
Research suggests that sleep may help the brain clear beta-amyloid, although the relationship between sleep and dementia remains complex and is still being studied.
HIV
Inflammation and infections can affect brain health. Untreated HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) can affect the central nervous system and is associated with HIV-related cognitive impairment.
"If you love and care for your brain, you're going to love your life a whole bunch more."
Amen said he has scanned "hundreds of people" with HIV, stating that the virus is "clearly a risk factor."

Untreated HIV is known to affect the central nervous system and is associated with HIV-related cognitive impairment. Effective antiretroviral therapy has greatly reduced the incidence of severe HIV-associated dementia.
Air pollution
Exposure to any toxins, from alcohol and marijuana to lead, mercury or air pollution, could be detrimental to brain health, according to Amen.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The WHO recommends reducing exposure to household and outdoor air pollution, particularly fine particulate matter. Research has linked long-term exposure to air pollution with a higher risk of cognitive decline and dementia, although the WHO characterizes the evidence as low to very low certainty.
Exposure to any toxins, from alcohol and marijuana to lead, mercury or air pollution, is detrimental to brain health, the doctor warned. (iStock)
Getting ahead of it
Dementia risk rises sharply with age. A recent U.S. analysis estimated that about one in five people had developed dementia by age 85, with risk increasing further at older ages.
While those with a genetic predisposition to the disease have a higher risk, Amen noted that certain lifestyle factors can increase the risk for anyone.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
"We should be on a dementia prevention program our whole lives," the doctor said. "It’s not something to start when you're 65."
Amen urged everyone to ask themselves the question: "Is what I’m doing good or bad for my brain?"
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
"Social activity is one of the prevention strategies. New learning is a prevention strategy," he added. "So always working on being connected with other people and then just making better decisions."
"If you love and care for your brain, you're going to love your life a whole bunch more."
Angelica Stabile is a lifestyle reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Sherrill anti-ICE policy hammered after fleeing migrant driver injures Dem mayor’s wife
summary: An illegal immigrant fled ICE agents and crashed into a Democratic mayor's wife on a New Jersey highway, reigniting the sanctuary state debate.
story: New Jersey State Sen. Mike Testa and Assemb. Paul Kanitra speak out to Fox News Digital over Gov. Mikie Sherrill's sanctuary policy and a Garden State Democrat's response calling for ICE to be abolished.

EXCLUSIVE: Sanctuary policies are leading to dangerous situations by making it harder for ICE to do its job, Republican critics argued after an illegal immigrant fled agents and crashed on a major New Jersey highway, injuring the wife of a Democratic mayor.

The Wednesday crash is fueling a renewed fight over New Jersey's limits on cooperation between local police and federal immigration authorities. Republicans are arguing Sherrill's approval of the "Trust Directive" creates public-safety risks by limiting the ability of ICE to work with police officers. They also contend that Democrats are wrongheaded to respond to such incidents by calling for ICE's abolition rather than stronger enforcement.

"This is just the latest in a long line of traffic incidents and vehicular incidents that wouldn't occur if New Jersey didn't have our sanctuary status that got codified as soon as Gov. Sherrill came into office," Assemblyman Paul Kanitra, R-Point Pleasant Beach, told Fox News Digital in an exclusive interview Friday.
DHS BOSS REVEALS OVAL OFFICE PLAN TO 'WITHHOLD FUNDING' FROM SANCTUARY CITIES AFTER AGGRESSIVE NEW YORK BUST
"Abolish ICE" has been a popular slogan among progressive activists. (Erik McGregor/LightRocket via Getty Images)
"We all fought against it. We told them that this would create chaos, and it seems like Democrats are unable to take accountability for their own actions."

Kanitra said Sherrill and other Democrats have been unable to recognize the connection between their support for the "Trust Directive" sanctuary policy — signed into law by the governor this year — and incidents such as the one in Middlesex County this week.
NJ TAXPAYERS ON THE HOOK FOR $12M MORE AS DEM GOVERNOR PROTECTS ILLEGAL ALIENS BATTLING DEPORTATION

Rye Barcott and Gov. Mikie Sherrill attend a conversation about Barcott's new book "Courage Will Save Us" with Gov. Wes Moore and Mark Drilling at 92NY on June 9, 2026, in New York City. (Dominik Bindl/Getty Images)

"Democrats seemingly have an inability to take accountability for their own actions here. They're unable to even recognize the chaos that they're creating, and they're shouting and screaming at everybody else trying to find somebody to blame. It's somewhat ridiculous," Kanitra said.
"You kind of reap what you sow," he said, adding that at least two people in his district have been killed in incidents connected to illegal immigrants behind the wheel.
DAD OF GIRL LEFT PERMANENTLY DISABLED IN CRASH WITH ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT RIPS DEMS: ‘I REJECT YOUR SYMPATHY’
Kanitra also pointed to a separate case in his county in which an illegal immigrant allegedly drove a vehicle into a family outside a kosher supermarket, killing an infant.
"They got behind the wheel, and they wound up killing an innocent toddler in the process," he said, calling the circumstances of the situation "absolutely abhorrent."
MAN FLEEING ICE OFFICERS IN FLORIDA IS STRUCK AND KILLED BY TRACTOR-TRAILER, POLICE SAY
Wednesday’s crash saw an illegal immigrant flee a targeted ICE operation, the agency told Fox News Digital, and speed off.
The suspect drove onto U.S. 130 — the heavily trafficked spine of the Trenton-Camden corridor — and collided with a Tesla in North Brunswick after running a stoplight.
FLEEING SUSPECT IN NEW JERSEY STRIKES ICE AGENT, WHO OPENS FIRE
One of the people injured in the other vehicle was the wife of East Brunswick Mayor Brad Cohen. Fox News Digital reached out to Cohen and North Brunswick Mayor Francis Womack III for comment.

"After repeated verbal warnings and due to officer safety concerns, ICE officers relied on their training and attempted to safely remove the illegal alien [from their car]. The illegal alien then proceeded to flee at a high rate of speed and collided with other vehicles," an ICE spokesperson confirmed to Fox News Digital.
HOCHUL BOASTS 'I JUST BANNED IT' AS NEW YORK OUTLAWS LOCAL POLICE PARTNERSHIPS WITH ICE

Sen. Mike Testa, R-Vineland, said Cape May County, one of the counties in his district, along with Monmouth County, fought hard but unsuccessfully against Sherrill and others to be able to engage with ICE through 287(g) interagency cooperation agreements.
The incident Wednesday showed why they are integral to keeping the public safe, he said.

"I think it has only emboldened illegal aliens to engage in illegal behavior. This illegal alien was stopped lawfully by federal authorities, ran through a red light, fleeing federal authorities and unfortunately ran into the mayor of East Brunswick's wife."

He said there has been little movement among Democratic leadership to address the troubling trend, but at least one member of the majority — Sen. Brian Stack, who is also the mayor of Union City — told him that, in an all-encompassing sense, laws on the books must be enforced.
Watson Coleman, whose district includes the area where the crash occurred, responded differently.
"Today, it appears an ICE involved car chase resulted in an accident involving the wife of the Mayor of East Brunswick. Abolish ICE," Rep. Bonnie Watson Coleman, D-N.J., tweeted.
SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Testa said that while Democrats’ "silence is deafening" writ-large, Watson Coleman’s call to abolish ICE shows that some Democrats are responding to the incident by targeting federal immigration enforcement rather than the driver.

"This is just another example of lawlessness. And sadly, there's been a stamp of approval from radical leftists like Congresswoman Bonnie Watson Coleman saying ICE should be abolished rather than actually punishing the criminal that put multiple citizens' lives at risk," he said.
Fox News Digital reached out to Watson Coleman and Sherrill for comment.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
As for his county's wish to forge a 287(g) agreement with ICE one day, he said it shows there are parts of the state that still believe in law and order.
"And we believe quite literally that citizenship should have its privileges. I've made this comment many times," he said.
Testa accused Watson Coleman and Sherrill of supporting policies that make it harder for federal authorities to arrest and remove illegal immigrants.
"You know, I'm a child of the '80s — and the old American Express commercial was ‘membership has its privileges’ — well, citizenship should have its privileges," he said.
Born and raised in Allentown, Pennsylvania, worked in both the New York and Washington bureaus for Fox News since 2013.

title: Sen Jim Justice finds way through Senate polarization to bring WWII hero memorial to DC
summary: Jim Justice reveals how a last-minute conversation with Martin Heinrich broke a partisan logjam to pass the Hershel Woody Williams monument bill.
story: In a wide-ranging interview, Sen. Jim Justice, R-W.Va., details how a private chat saved a national monument bill, shares his candid views on Washington’s partisan gridlock.
Sen. Jim Justice, R-W.Va., found a way to get something passed unanimously, despite what he rebukes as "romper-room behavior" of political polarization in the Senate.

In an interview Saturday with Fox News Digital, Justice detailed how he worked around the Senate’s bitter partisan divide to get a monument honoring late World War II Medal of Honor hero Hershel "Woody" Williams onto the National Mall.

"I've never seen anything like this, never in my life seen anything to where it is, it is so preposterous," Justice lamented. "You know, no one could make any sense out of what in the world is going on a lot of times."
"I don't know why we don't talk to one another," he added. "I don't know why we're disrespectful to one other."
DEMOCRATS BLINK AS SCHUMER HELPS GOP CLEAR KEY SHUTDOWN HURDLE

Congressional Medal of Honor recipient Hershel Woody Williams salutes while standing at the new Gold Star Families Memorial Monument in downtown Pensacola on Tuesday, Nov. 10, 2020. (Gregg Pachkowski/Imagn)

Using good, old-fashioned dialogue, Justice's effort ultimately succeeded in getting his first Senate law passed for his late friend. The Williams National Medal of Honor Monument Location Act directs the National Medal of Honor monument to a prominent location within the Reserve on the National Mall.

The legislation is Justice’s first bill as a senator. It honors Williams, a West Virginia native who received the Medal of Honor for extraordinary heroism during the Battle of Iwo Jima and who was the last surviving World War II Medal of Honor recipient before his death in 2022 at age 98. The monument will honor Williams by name while commemorating Medal of Honor recipients as a whole.
The House approved the measure on Aug. 31 after the Senate passed it unanimously in March. The legislation is now awaiting Trump’s signature.
"We're really hopeful he's going to sign it this coming week," Justice said. "There's been a lot to make all that happen and everything, and I can't be more proud."
Justice, describing the partisan fight in the interview, said the path to unanimous approval was anything but smooth.
EXCLUSIVE: NEW AMERICA 250 MONUMENT LETS FAMILIES FIND MILITARY RELATIVES IN SECONDS: 'I HAD TEARS IN MY EYES'

Hershel "Woody" Williams, shown here at Slugger Field in Louisville, Ky. on Aug. 22, 2021, was the last living Medal of Honor recipient from World War II before he passed away June 29, 2022, at the age of 98. (Sam Upshaw Jr./Courier Journal / USA TODAY NETWORK)
"I mean, we had it shot down," he said, adding, but "I just wouldn’t turn it loose."

"And the reason I wouldn’t turn loose is because it was just real simple: I mean Woody’s unbelievable, or was unbelievable, that’s for sure. But all these Medal of Honor recipients and everything, the ones we’ve lost and all those that are still living, they are so deserving."
Justice described how the measure initially had become caught up in the same divisiveness that has locked up the Senate on a much broader range of issues.

"All we managed to do is keep a food fight going to where – because it was a Republican thing or Republican Jim Justice introducing – well, I’m telling you, if I’m a Democrat, by God, we’re not gonna let that happen and everything," he lamented. "And then it’s just, it’s the same thing on both sides. Way, way, way too much for a guy that’s got white hair and wants to try to get things done."
EXCAVATION SET TO BEGIN ON TRUMP ADMINISTRATION'S 250-FOOT TRIUMPHAL ARCH AMID LEGAL BATTLE
Sen. Jim Justice, R-W.Va., and English bulldog, Babydog, combined to work a bipartisan bill pass unanimously in the bitterly divided Senate. (Office of Senator Jim Justice)
Justice said the breakthrough came just before he was preparing to take the matter to the Senate floor with four Medal of Honor recipients present.
"I was about three feet from going into the Senate chambers," Justice recalled. "And we sat down right there, you know, kind of on the steps and really just started talking."

The senator was Sen. Martin Heinrich, D-N.M. The two serve together on the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, and Justice said he had developed a personal relationship with Heinrich over the years, including through Justice’s well-known bulldog, Babydog.
SEN RICK SCOTT: AMERICANS WORK FIVE DAYS A WEEK, WHY CAN’T THE SENATE?
Members of Congress pay respects to Chief Warrant Officer 4 Hershel Woodrow "Woody" Williams as his remains lie in honor in the Capitol Rotunda in Washington on July 14, 2022. (Tom Williams)

"I said, Martin, I don’t understand. I mean, how in the world can we do this?" Justice said. "And I said, Martin, you know, I’m getting ready to go on the floor, and it’s not going to be good. It’s not gonna be good for you. It’s not going to good for a lot of folks and everything. A lot of people are going to be upset. A lot of people are going to be really sad."
Justice said he appealed directly to Heinrich to find a way forward.
"And I just said, Martin, I don’t know any way to tell it other than just to tell you the truth. And you’re a good guy. And I don’t know why in the world we just can’t talk with one another."
Heinrich responded with a blunt explanation of the broader problem, Justice said.
MEDAL OF HONOR RECIPIENT JAMES CAPERS JR. SAYS RECOGNITION IS BITTERSWEET AFTER LOSING 'SO MUCH'

The coffin of Hershel Woodrow "Woody" Williams is carried down the East Front Center Steps of the U.S. Capitol during a ceremony after lying in honor in Washington, D.C., on July 14, 2022. (Anna Rose Layden)
"And he looked right at me, and he said, you know, people here don’t talk to one another," Justice said. "And I really appreciate you doing that, and I’m not going to object."
Justice said the measure then moved "in three minutes, boom, boom, boom, done."
"It was an amazing moment really, and like I said, Martin's a good guy, and I just think that maybe we could all learn from that just a little bit," he said.
"Now we're going to honor, you know, another great, unbelievable, courageous group of people, and it's way, way, way overdue."
HOUSE REPUBLICANS DID WHAT VOTERS ASKED AND WE HAVE THE RECEIPTS. IT’S UP TO THE SENATE

Thousands of fans flooded onto the National Mall for the Freedom 250 Grand Prix, many getting their first taste of IndyCar or even live motorsports in general. (Photo by Hasan Akbas/Anadolu via Getty Images)
On other issues in the Senate still in gridlock, Justice urged dialogue like that above and for everyone to "grow up."

"Why in the world would you carry on with just childishness, and in all fairness, that's what it is," Justice said. "You can't make sense of it. There's no point in us trying to do that. This is Romper Room behavior. And if there's anything in the world I could do, I wish to goodness that I could tell everybody, you know let's grow up a lot. Let's absolutely grow up and let's behave."

Justice said he does not expect the Senate’s structural problems to be fixed easily, pointing to the 60-vote threshold associated with overcoming a filibuster and arguing that lawmakers have little incentive to change a system that protects the political status quo.
HEGSETH UPGRADES ABBEY GATE MARINES' VALOR AWARDS AFTER 5-YEAR DELAY: 'THOSE DAYS ARE OVER'
Sen. Martin Heinrich, D-N.M., was one of the key members of the left to help get Sen. Jim Justice's Hershel Woody Williams bill passed unanimously in the Senate. (Elizabeth Frantz)
"You’ve got a lot of people there that have never had a job," Justice said. "They’ve been there forever, and they’ve never made a payroll."
He said his former chief of staff Brian Abraham once gave him an even simpler explanation for the paralysis.

"I said, ‘guys, we’re really missing something here because we can really get stuff done here and everything,’" Justice recalled. "And he looked right at me, and he said, ‘you don’t understand, do you?’

"People here don’t wanna get something done. All they want to do is just keep it going. Round and round it goes. Fundraiser, fundraiser, fundraiser. Round and around it goes, get reelected, get re-elected."
DAKOTA MEYER TALKS SERVICE, BLASTS CONTROVERSIAL DESIGN FOR GLOBAL WAR ON TERROR MEMORIAL
Justice said the monument fight was especially important because Williams himself embodied the opposite of that kind of self-interest.
"Woody Williams was all about us," he said. "Woody Williams was never about Woody Williams. And he just was an amazing man. I got to know him really well, and we became really good friends."

Williams’ Medal of Honor citation stems from his actions on Iwo Jima, where, under intense enemy fire, he used a flamethrower to destroy Japanese positions and help clear a path for advancing Marines.
Justice said the symbolism of the monument extends beyond Williams and into future generations.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"Now, I’m going to take them there," Justice said of his future descendants. "I’m going to show them this and tell them, maybe I was only a grain of sand, but I had something to do with this. And I really stood up hard for it and everything. We got it done."

Eric Mack is a breaking news reporter and writer Sunday through Thursday, 6 a.m. ET to 2 p.m. ET, with a particular interest in stories that lead the news cycle on politics, elections, foreign affairs and government.

title: Israel's ambassador says NYC’s Mamdani is ‘sowing chaos’ ahead of Netanyahu’s UN appearance
summary: Israel's U.N. Ambassador Danny Danon said "instead of actually welcoming all world leaders," NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani is "doing exactly the opposite."
story: Israel’s U.N. Ambassador Danny Danon previews to Fox News Digital the upcoming visit by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to the U.N. General Assembly.

Israeli Ambassador to the United Nations Danny Danon told Fox News Digital that New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is "sowing chaos" ahead of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s visit to the U.N. General Assembly later this month.
Danon made the remark after Mamdani called on New Yorkers in July to protest when Netanyahu arrives to speak at the general debate at U.N. headquarters on Sept. 24.
"No one can ignore Mayor Mamdani, you know, instead of actually welcoming all world leaders and making sure that the city will function properly, he is doing exactly the opposite," Danon said.

"He is inciting, he is sowing chaos into the city. So this year, unfortunately, it will be harder for every New Yorker or every visitor because the mayor is actually calling for people to go out, to demonstrate and it will not deter us. The prime minister will come, will speak and will represent our nation," the ambassador added.
ISRAELI PM BENJAMIN NETANYAHU VOWS TO VISIT NEW YORK DESPITE MAMDANI'S REPEATED CALLS FOR HIS ARREST
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, left, and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. (Kyle Mazza/Anadolu via Getty Images; Ronen Zvulun/Pool/AFP via Getty Images)
Mamdani’s office, when asked by Fox News Digital if he had any plans to meet with Netanyahu while he is in town, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
"I don't think the prime minister wants to meet with him," Danon said.

Mamdani previously called Netanyahu a "war criminal" and "architect of a horrific genocide against the Palestinian people." The Democratic socialist also acknowledged that he can't have Netanyahu arrested despite promising to do so during his mayoral campaign.

When asked by a reporter in July about "What do you think that these people who are frustrated with Netanyahu should do when he arrives in New York City for the United Nations meeting," Mamdani said, "One of the bedrocks of our city is protest."

"It is something that has been a part of what makes our city so special, that New Yorkers can express themselves whether they are in support or in opposition no matter on whatever topic," the Democratic socialist mayor said during the press conference on July 22. "And I’ve always said that when we respect our Constitution, we also respect our First Amendment. And here in New York City it will always be a place where you can exercise that."
IRAN TRIED TO ASSASSINATE ONE OF NETANYAHU'S SONS, PRIME MINISTER SAYS

Ambassador Danny Danon of Israel attends the monthly Security Council meeting on the situation in the Middle East, at U.N. Headquarters in New York on Aug. 11, 2026. (Pacific Press/LightRocket via Getty Images)

Netanyahu told Fox News "Hannity" around a week later that, "I’m going to New York," and, "I'm going to speak the truth in front of this hate-spewing elected official who's pitting one group of New Yorkers against the others."
Danon told Fox News Digital that "we have been involved in a war, a difficult one, a long one, and I think now we have a lot of opportunities ahead of us."
"So the prime minister would also speak about what we achieved, but also about the opportunities," he said.
Danon also said Israel has to "finish the job" in Gaza.

"Hamas is still there. They are supposed to disarm, according to the president's plan. I hope it will take place. I hope that it will happen sooner than later because if it will not happen, we will have to do the job ourselves. But we cannot leave a terrorist organization in Gaza. There will be no future for the people of Gaza or for us if Hamas will stay in power," he continued.
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) speaking at a press conference in Manhattan Housing Court in New York City on Aug. 25, 2026. (Michael Brochstein/Sipa USA via Reuters Connect)

"I think we can be very proud of our achievements. Israel is being criticized, but we walk very proud at the U.N. because we know that what we did, fighting evil, fighting Iran, fighting Hezbollah, fighting Hamas, it wasn't only our fight. We fought for the Western societies, for the Western democracies," Danon also said. "That's why we feel proud on what we achieved this year."

title: Trump appears to debut darker hair, sparking online buzz
summary: New photos of President Trump stepping off Air Force One with what appeared to be a darker hairstyle have quickly fueled social media buzz.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

President Donald Trump appeared to debut a darker hair color Friday, sparking widespread speculation online after stepping off Air Force One in New Jersey ahead of a weekend at his Bedminster golf club.

Known for his signature blond hairstyle, Trump was photographed arriving at Morristown Municipal Airport with what appeared to be a noticeably darker, more brunette look —prompting a flood of reactions across social media.
"Trump becoming a brunette was definitely not on my 2026 bingo card," one user wrote on X.
"This was Donald Trump yesterday while departing to New Jersey for the weekend! Look at the appearance of his hair! Is he getting a new hair color?" another user wrote.
HOUSE DEMS PLOT TRUMP INVESTIGATION BLITZ IF THEY SEIZE MAJORITY
President Donald Trump waves to reporters while stepping off Air Force One at Morristown Municipal Airport in Morristown, New Jersey on Sept. 4, 2026. (Jim WATSON / AFP via Getty Images)
"Seems brown is the new blonde ...," a third user added.
"Trump is now a brunette!" another post read.

Photos shared on Instagram by internet personality Michael Solakiewicz showed Trump golfing Saturday in a red hat that covered most of his hair, making it difficult to tell whether the darker look remained.
TRUMP’S PENTAGON SHAKE-UP REVIVES A PRESIDENTIAL POWER PLAY WITH A LONG HISTORY
Trump has rarely made noticeable changes to his appearance while in office. (Jim WATSON / AFP via Getty Images)
The online speculation comes just days after Trump pushed back on allegations that he wears a wig, pointing to a windy 2024 campaign rally in Ohio, according to The Hill.
"I don’t wear a wig. But that night, they found out I did not wear a wig because if you did, it was not going to be on your head very long," Trump said Wednesday.
Trump has rarely made noticeable changes to his appearance while in office.
TRUMP NEGOTIATORS WITKOFF, KUSHNER MEET WITH PUTIN IN MOSCOW AS US PUSHES FOR END TO RUSSIA-UKRAINE WAR
In 2019, Trump sparked similar speculation after appearing with what looked like a slicked-back hairstyle during a visit to a Virginia church. (JIM WATSON/AFP via Getty Images)

In 2019, he sparked similar speculation after appearing with what looked like a slicked-back hairstyle during a surprise visit to a Virginia church.
That hairstyle was short-lived. Trump spoke to reporters later in the day wearing his usual hairdo.

title: Pistol-packing man knocks over fairgoers forcing his way toward Ohio governor candidate Amy Acton, police say
summary: Amy Acton's campaign says the Ohio governor candidate was targeted by an armed individual at the Canfield Fair as political violence fears mount.
story: Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy explores the normalization of political violence in America and the root causes on ‘The Will Cain Show.’
An armed man forced his way through a crowd toward Ohio gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton, knocking over multiple fairgoers before troopers stopped him at the Canfield Fair, authorities said.

Troopers assigned to the Ohio State Highway Patrol’s executive protection unit intercepted Patrick M. Havas, 38, during the Sept. 6 incident, according to a statement provided by the Ohio Department of Public Safety to Fox News Digital.

"Havas knocked multiple fairgoers over while trying to get towards Dr. Acton, and was found to be in possession of a taser and two pistols," the highway patrol said. "Dr. Acton was unharmed during the incident."
Havas was turned over first to Canfield Fair Police and then to the Mahoning County Sheriff’s Office before being taken to the county jail, according to the statement.
TRUMP'S DECADE OF ASSASSINATION THREATS RUNS FROM BUTLER SHOOTING TO LATEST GOLF CLUB BREACH

Patrick M. Havas, 38, was charged with two counts of assault and disorderly conduct after authorities say he forced his way through a crowd toward Ohio gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton. (Mahoning County Sheriff's Office)
He was booked on two counts of assault and one count of disorderly conduct. A jail record listed Havas as being held in pretrial custody.
The highway patrol and sheriff’s office are investigating what led to the confrontation. No additional details were immediately available.
Acton’s campaign initially said an armed individual had lunged at the candidate and injured multiple people.
"While attending the Canfield Fair, an armed individual lunged at Dr. Acton, injuring multiple people," Acton campaign communications director Addie Bullock said in a statement.

"Dr. Acton and Eric are grateful for the swift and decisive action of law enforcement and are praying for the recovery of those injured," Bullock added. "This kind of violence has no place in Ohio. Dr. Acton will always stand up to the chaos, hate and vitriol that pits us against one another."

Amy Acton, former director of the Ohio Department of Health and Democratic gubernatorial candidate, meets with local residents while campaigning at Bottoms Up Coffee in Columbus, Ohio, on Monday, April 6, 2026. (Stephen Zenner/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine later confirmed that Acton was not hurt and said he and first lady Fran DeWine spoke with her following the incident.

"Fran and I are thankful Dr. Amy Acton was not hurt, and we send our thoughts to those who were injured," DeWine said. "We spoke to Dr. Acton this afternoon and she said to share with Ohioans that she is ok."
DeWine said a man "tried to forcefully push himself toward Dr. Acton" as she was speaking and injured other attendees at the Mahoning County Democratic booth.
"We are grateful for the quick work of the Ohio State Highway Patrol and other law enforcement on the scene at the Canfield Fair today," the governor said.
"Violence or the threat of violence at political or public events is always unacceptable," DeWine added. "This case is now in the hands of law enforcement and will be investigated thoroughly."
Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine speaks during a news conference, Friday, Dec. 29, 2023, in Columbus, Ohio.  (AP Photo/Carolyn Kaster)
The incident came as Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin warned that candidates and other public figures continue to face threats as campaign season kicks into high gear.
"You’re never safe in the public eye," Mullin told Fox News’ Peter Doocy during an interview on "The Sunday Briefing."
WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENTS’ DINNER SHOOTING LATEST IN YEARS OF ATTACKS TARGETING TRUMP, CONSERVATIVES

In a show of solidarity, Ohio gubernatorial hopeful Amy Acton stood alongside striking members of United Steelworkers Local 3057 outside the ArcelorMittal steel plant. Acton had to shout over passing motorists honking their horns and showing support for the steelworkers in Cleveland, Ohio, on Feb. 2, 2026. (Jason J. Molyet/News Journal / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images)

Doocy asked Mullin whether candidates were safe heading into the traditional Labor Day weekend kickoff to campaign season, citing the political assassinations and assassination attempts that have rocked the country in recent years.
"If you read any of the social media posts, which I choose not to, but you see the type of rhetoric and the hatefulness that’s out there," Mullin said.
DEM SENATE HOPEFULS UNDER SCRUTINY FOR ‘CHOKE THEM OUT’ RHETORIC AFTER TRUMP ATTACK SCARE

Markwayne Mullin, secretary of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), during a cabinet meeting at the White House in Washington, DC, on Thursday, March 26, 2026.  (Will Oliver/EPA/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
"The threats to our elected officials, they don’t go away," he continued. "We’ve got to bring down the temperature, but the temperature is not going to go down on itself."
Mullin said Americans must accept that political disagreements are part of the country’s system of government while drawing a firm line at violence.
WEST VIRGINIA MAN PLEADS GUILTY TO MAKING VIOLENT THREATS AGAINST TRUMP, ICE
"The American people have to realize that we do have a republic, and the republic has different opinions, and it’s OK to have different opinions," he said.

"When you cross a line and say that that different opinion needs to be silenced — it needs to be silenced through violence — that’s where Homeland comes into place," Mullin added. "Free speech is something we all protect, but there’s a line that you can cross that goes from free speech to inciting dangerous behavior."
Mullin was speaking broadly about political threats and was not responding directly to the reported confrontation involving Acton.
Republican gubernatorial nominee Vivek Ramaswamy and his running mate, Ohio Senate President Rob McColley, condemned the Canfield Fair incident.
"Candidates should be able to meet with voters without having to worry about threats or violence," Ramaswamy campaign communications director Connie Luck said in a statement.
"What happened today is completely unacceptable and has no place in politics, and we hope that no one was hurt," she added.
RAMASWAMY OUTLINES KEY CONTRASTS WITH DEM OPPONENT LESS THAN 100 DAYS OUT FROM KEY GUBERNATORIAL ELECTION
Ohio republican guebenatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy speaks during a campaign rally on February 25, 2025, at the Glass City Center in Toledo, Ohio. (Scott W. Grau/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)
Acton and Ramaswamy are facing off in November’s closely watched race to replace term-limited Republican Gov. Mike DeWine.

Acton, a physician, became a household name in Ohio while serving as director of the Ohio Department of Health during the COVID-19 pandemic, according to The Associated Press. She appeared alongside DeWine during televised briefings as the state imposed shutdowns and other public-health restrictions.

Her handling of the pandemic has since become a central campaign issue, The AP reported. Ramaswamy and other Republicans have criticized Acton over the restrictions, while her campaign has defended her work with DeWine as necessary to protect Ohioans.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Mahoning County Sheriff’s Office for additional information.
Fox News' Peter Doocy contributed to this report.
Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

title: Hasan Piker brushes off Dems who see him as a liability, names his '28 choice
summary: Hasan Piker told Fox News his job isn't to help the Democratic Party, even as consultant James Carville called him "an idiot" who isn't a Democrat.
story: Far-left influencer Hasan Piker explains why Democrats should study the boldness of President Donald Trump and the MAGA movement.
Hasan Piker hears the growing chorus of Democrats condemning him for incendiary statements, and he has a message for the party: "My job is not to make the Democratic Party look good."

The far-left Twitch streamer has boosted socialist candidates even as he created headaches for the broader Democratic Party in a midterm election cycle where it hopes to make major gains. The 35-year-old Piker — whose polarizing stances range from defending communist Chinese dictator Mao Zedong to comparing Zionism to "Nazism" — is a darling of the Democratic Socialists of America, but a potential liability for mainstream Democrats as November approaches.
Piker said Democratic Party officials have not reached out to coordinate a strategy.
"I have not had a conversation with anyone from the DNC," Piker said. "That would be very funny."
JAMES CARVILLE DECRIES 'IDIOT' HASAN PIKER, ORDERS DSA TO CHANGE ITS NAME

In an exclusive interview at the 2026 Socialism Conference in Chicago, Piker told Fox News that, while he tries "to be as careful as possible" when it comes to choosing his words, his hours-long streams present his opponents with the "perfect opportunity to create viral media moments."
Twitch streamer Hasan Piker appeared on the campaign trail with Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo)
Some of those moments include intense backlash over Piker’s 2019 statement that America "deserved 9/11," a comment which has been widely condemned by politicians on both sides of the aisle.
HASAN PIKER CALLS REPUBLICAN PARTY THE 'BIGGEST DOMESTIC TERRORIST' IN THE COUNTRY
Piker acknowledged that he should not have used the word "deserved," but said his point was that "[America’s] meddling in the affairs in the Middle East actually transpired these horrifying events."
"It's not a controversial thing [to argue]," Piker said. "It was the language that I used that was controversial."
HASAN PIKER CALLS HAMAS 'FAR MORE MODERATE,' DISMISSES TERROR GROUP’S BRUTAL RULE IN GAZA
Piker's brash commentary gives him credence with the far-left DSA, which pulled off a host of primary victories against more moderate Democrats, but party elders have disavowed him.
Democratic strategist James Carville sharply criticized far-left Democrats for targeting longtime incumbents in primary elections in a video posted Friday for Politicon. (Politicon/YouTube)

"There’s two things that I know about Hasan Piker," longtime Democratic Party consultant James Carville told Fox News Channel last week. "One, he’s an idiot, and two, he’s not a Democrat. So, I don’t answer for idiots, and I don’t answer for people who are not Democrats."
VAN JONES WARNS FAR-LEFT SOCIALIST AGENDA IS 'REGRESSIVE' THREAT TO DEMOCRATIC PARTY
Key Democrat lawmakers, including House Minority Leader Hakeen Jeffries, senators Cory Booker, D-N.J., and Jon Ossoff, D-Ga., and several House members have condemned Piker's past rhetoric.

As he crosses the country, joining campaign rallies and canvass launches for liberal challengers to establishment-backed candidates, Piker acknowledged that even his allies have urged him to moderate his rhetoric for the sake of their electoral chances.
DEMOCRATS' CIVIL WAR HEADS TO MICHIGAN WHERE PROGRESSIVES FACE BIGGEST TEST YET IN HIGH-STAKES SENATE SHOWDOWN

But Piker told Fox News the press is overstating his association with the progressive political candidates and wondered why the media had not "demanded condemnations from establishment Republicans for collaborating with Charlie Kirk or using him as a campaign surrogate."

Piker campaigned hard for Abdul El-Sayed, the progressive Michigan Democratic Senate nominee who pulled off a major upset victory against the establishment-backed Rep. Haley Stevens, D- Mich., in August. While his active support for El-Sayed may have generated buzz among Piker's base, it's also led El-Sayed to face a barrage of questions and criticism about his association with Piker.
GRETCHEN WHITMER ENDORSES MODERATE HALEY STEVENS IN TIGHT UPCOMING SENATE PRIMARY

Piker said that while he is confident El-Sayed – who distanced himself from Piker in recent weeks – will win this fall, "if people want to blame me" in the event El-Sayed loses, "they can blame me," adding, "I think that's the goal."
Hasan Piker named Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez as his preferred presidential candidate over a slate of high-profile Democrats. (Getty Images)

Piker's role in the midterms may prove to be a warmup for the 2028 presidential election, and he said he has no plans to moderate his stances or stay on the sidelines. He said he will back socialist Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y. if she launches a bid for the Democratic Party's presidential nomination.
WATCH: AOC WON'T RULE OUT WHITE HOUSE BID AFTER POLL NAMES HER DEMOCRATS' TOP 2028 PICK
"I think she's great," Piker said. "She would have some difficulties, of course, but hurdles can be climbed over, and I think she can do it."
Piker believes his influence will continue to grow, and predicted even Democrats now condemning him will "try to utilize the platform that I have" if they seek higher office in 2028.
2028 BATTLEGROUND POLL SCRAMBLES DEMOCRATS’ FUTURE AS INSURGENT SOCIALIST SEIZES LEAD

"And I'm not talking about my ideological allies or people who are associated with me right now," he added.
Matthew Donnell is a Campaign Embed at FOX News and an Assignment Editor at FOX Business.

title: After 'Lake America,' Trump suggests a new name for the state of New Mexico
summary: The White House reposted Trump's Truth Social image showing New Mexico crossed out and rebranded as "America" days after the Lake America order.
story: Donald Trump renames Lake Ontario as 'Lake America' amid escalating trade tensions with Canada, declaring that the neighboring country has been ripping off the United States. Senior White House correspondent Peter Doocy reports on the Canadian response to the symbolic change.

The White House on Sunday amplified President Donald Trump's call to rebrand New Mexico as "New America," reposting an image from the president's Truth Social account showing the state's name crossed out and replaced with "America."
Trump's original post featured a map of the Southwestern state with the word "Mexico" crossed out in bright red and replaced with "America," effectively depicting it as "New America."
TRUMP RENAMES LAKE ONTARIO ‘LAKE AMERICA’ AMID INTENSIFYING US-CANADA TRADE DISPUTE
The White House later shared the image on its verified X account. Neither post included an explanation or indicated whether it reflected an actual policy proposal.
New Mexico Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham told Fox News Digital that New Mexico's name "isn't up for debate — it's been ours since before the United States existed."

"What is up for debate? Who's showing up for working families," she said, arguing that while the president "tries to distract Americans," families are facing higher gas and grocery prices, losing access to health care and struggling to afford a home.

"Under Democratic leadership here in New Mexico, we’re providing families with free childcare and college, protecting access to health care and investing in housing. While the White House wastes time coloring on maps, Nuevo México is busy doing the work."
MAJORITY OF AMERICANS REJECT TRUMP'S RENAMING OF LAKE ONTARIO TO 'LAKE AMERICA,' POLL FINDS
President Donald Trump signs an executive order to rename Lake Ontario as "Lake America" during an event in the Oval Office of the White House on Thursday. (Getty Images)

The post comes just days after Trump signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario "Lake America" for U.S. federal use. The executive order followed a series of tariff disputes between Washington and Ottawa.

Trump said he directed Interior Secretary Doug Burgum and the department to update the Geographic Names Information System to reflect the name change. Google and Apple later updated their maps for U.S. users to reflect the change.
Trump also signed an executive order renaming the Gulf of Mexico the "Gulf of America" early in his second term.

Unlike lakes and other geographic features that can be renamed for federal use through executive action, a president cannot unilaterally rename a U.S. state. Trump and the White House have not announced any formal effort to change New Mexico's name.

The name "New Mexico" predates the state by centuries. Spanish explorers began using "Nuevo México" in the late 1500s. The territory kept the name after becoming part of the United States in 1848 and later achieved statehood on Jan. 6, 1912.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
President Donald Trump posted a map showing New Mexico relabeled as "New America." The White House later reposted the image on X. (Al Drago/Getty Images)
The White House did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.
Amanda Macias covers the intersection of business, economics and politics, with a focus on how policy decisions shape markets, businesses and American workers.

title: Trump admin’s mail-in ballot fight lands back at Supreme Court
summary: The Trump administration asks the Supreme Court to enforce postal service ballot mail restrictions as North Carolina ballots already enter the mail.
story: Fox News legal editor Kerri Urbahn joins 'Fox & Friends' to analyze lawsuits filed by 24 states and Washington, D.C. against the United States Postal Service regarding mail-in voting rules. Urbahn breaks down the Supreme Court decision and details agency rules requiring barcodes on mail-in ballots.

The Trump administration filed a new appeal with the Supreme Court on Sunday seeking to enforce restrictions on mail ballots, as the ballots begin entering states across the country ahead of the midterm elections.

The filing asks the high court to stay a preliminary injunction issued Friday by U.S. District Court Judge Indira Talwani that prevents the U.S. Postal Service from enforcing several requirements for ballot mail in the November elections.

"Ballots have already begun to be mailed in North Carolina, and more States will begin the mailing process as the injunction remains in place — including Alabama on September 9 and at least five States the week of September 13," Solicitor General John Sauer wrote.
FEDERAL JUDGE AGAIN BLOCKS TRUMP'S MAIL BALLOT ORDER JUST BEFORE MIDTERMS
Envelopes for mail-in ballots at the Wake County Board of Elections are seen on Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026, in Raleigh, N.C. (AP Photo/Matt Ramey)
"Once those ballot envelopes enter the mailstream, there is no retrieving them," he added.

Sauer argued that allowing the injunction to remain in place risks "sowing confusion and chaos" as more states begin mailing ballots because preparations to comply with the Postal Service rule remain voluntary rather than mandatory.
The administration maintains the rule is "a lawful and modest exercise of rulemaking authority delegated by Congress to the Postal Service" and "regulates the U.S. Mail, not federal elections."
Wake County Board of Elections employees prepare absentee ballots to be mailed on Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026, in Raleigh, N.C. (AP Photo/Matt Ramey)

The rule requires federal election ballots sent through the mail to use envelopes that include the official Election Mail logo, meet automation requirements and carry unique barcodes, according to the filing. State election officials would also have to submit envelope designs for review and provide the Postal Service with information about intended ballot recipients.
The administration says the requirements are intended to improve the handling and delivery of ballot mail and protect the mail system from being used to facilitate voter fraud.
MAIL-VOTING CRACKDOWN MOVES AHEAD AS TRUMP COURT WIN OPENS DOOR TO FEDERAL ACTION

The rule would not give the Postal Service authority to determine who is eligible to vote by mail or whether ballots should be counted, responsibilities that would remain with state and local election officials.

Democratic-led states and voting rights groups challenging the restrictions contend the changes are unconstitutional, while election officials have argued there is not enough time to revise their systems to comply before November.
A large box of pre-assembled mail-in ballots at the Wake County Board of Elections on Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026, in Raleigh, N.C. (AP Photo/Matt Ramey)

The administration disputes those arguments, saying Congress gave the Postal Service broad authority to regulate the handling and delivery of mail and that the rule does not dictate ballot content, determine voter eligibility, establish election deadlines or govern how ballots are counted.

The filing marks the third time the administration has asked the Supreme Court to intervene in the dispute. The high court previously allowed the administration’s plan to move forward but has not ruled on whether the restrictions themselves are legal.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The battle could have major ramifications for the November elections, when control of Congress is at stake. Nearly one-third of U.S. voters cast ballots by mail.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Sanders pushes 'death penalty' for crucial US industry that could give advantage to foreign adversaries
summary: Progressives on Capitol Hill are pushing a proposal to ban artificial superintelligence, but critics warn the move could hand global tech dominance over to China and Russia.
story: Bridget Bean, former CISA executive director, warns that China is rapidly closing the A.I. gap, raising concerns about its 'dystopian' models and cyber-biological weapon risks. She stresses the importance of U.S. innovation and protecting advanced chip technology to maintain global leadership.

Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and Rep. Greg Casar, D-Texas, introduced legislation Thursday seeking to hit American artificial intelligence developers with a "corporate death penalty" and up to 20 years in prison— a move critics warn will hand a crucial edge in the global AI arms race to Beijing and Moscow.

The Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act would temporarily halt advanced AI development and establish a Cabinet-level federal agency authorized to oversee the physical destruction of non-compliant tech systems, likening advanced AI creation to the unlawful development of nuclear weapons. The measure explicitly targets systems capable of matching or exceeding human cognitive performance—specifically outlawing any AI model that exhibits the capacity to subvert shutdown commands, execute unauthorized cyberattacks, or undermine the U.S. government.

But while progressives frame the measure as an urgent check on "AI oligarchs," experts are warning that imposing sweeping criminal penalties on U.S. firms will severely handicap domestic innovation, while foreign adversaries will be able to continue expanding their capabilities unchecked.
FETTERMAN ALIGNS WITH TRUMP ON AI PUSH, WARNS CHINA BENEFITS FROM US 'OVERREACTION'

A newly proposed bill from progressive lawmakers seeks to ban the development of artificial superintelligence, threatening U.S. developers with extreme criminal penalties. (Oliver Berg/picture alliance via Getty Images)

"If the United States stops developing advanced AI, China is unlikely to follow. Surrendering the lead in a potentially transformative technology would carry serious economic and national security costs," Daniel Castro, president of the Information Technology and Innovation Foundation (ITIF), a leading nonpartisan tech-innovation policy think tank, said in response to Sanders' proposal.

"A permanent, unilateral ban on all research into superhuman AI is too broad," added Gary Marcus, an AI expert who has testified on the matter before the U.S. Senate. He added that the proposed law was "a guarantee" the U.S. would be left behind when it comes to artificial intelligence advancements, describing it as "not the right approach," even though he said there were some aspects of the proposed bill that were "defensible."
REP. TED LIEU: AI IS ALREADY TOO POWERFUL. WE NEED A KILL SWITCH BEFORE DISASTER STRIKES

Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., speaks during a news conference on the impact of artificial intelligence on workers at the Hart Senate Office Building on April 16, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Heather Diehl/Getty Images)
Under the provisions of the legislation, the proposed criminal and corporate penalties are modeled directly after existing federal statutes governing the unlawful development of nuclear weapons.

Tech companies found attempting to circumvent the federal prohibition would face a "corporate death penalty"—an unprecedented enforcement mechanism that strips a firm's legal authority to conduct business in the United States. Individual software engineers, researchers or executives found in violation could face up to 20 years in federal prison.
DEM SENATOR PRESSES OPENAI, ANTHROPIC FOR ANSWERS IN AI HACKING PROBE

To enforce the ban, the legislation creates a new Cabinet-level federal AI agency tasked with monitoring frontier systems. The agency would be granted sweeping authority to intervene in tech operations, including physically supervising the removal of dangerous code and overseeing the physical destruction of non-compliant superintelligent hardware and infrastructure.

The bill also establishes criteria for what constitutes a banned system, specifically outlawing any AI model capable of planning or executing the "disempowerment of humanity." That includes software that exhibits the capacity to overthrow the U.S. government, carry out unauthorized cyberattacks or ignore human shutdown commands.
CRACKDOWN ON CRITICAL TECH COULD OPEN AMERICANS TO A NEW NATIONAL SECURITY THREAT
Rep. Greg Casar, D-Texas, speaks during the news conference inside the U.S. Capitol on July 16, 2025. (Bill Clark/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)
Industry advocates, however, argue that resorting to extreme criminal sanctions ignores the practical realities of tech infrastructure and risk management.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"Knee-jerk policymaking is never a good thing, and I think that’s exactly what this proposal boils down to," said Aden Hizkias, associate policy director at Chamber of Progress, a tech industry coalition. "AI is an incredible tool that can improve millions of lives, but as AI skepticism grows, it’s on companies to earn trust and prove they are good neighbors. That means transparent construction agreements, bringing their own power generation, and making sure they're meeting environmental standards."

Fox News Digital reached out to Sanders' office for comment regarding concerns that the legislation would hand an AI edge to foreign adversaries like China and Russia, but did not receive a response in time for publication.
Alec Schemmel is a Politics Reporter for Fox News Digital who is originally from Charlotte, North Carolina but now resides in the Washington D.C.-Baltimore Metro Area.

title: Mamdani under fire after symbolic 9/11 pen goes to former al Qaeda defense lawyer
summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani faces backlash for handing a 9/11 ceremonial pen to aide Ramzi Kassem, who represented a convicted al Qaeda member.
story: 9/11 families are calling for NYC Mayor Mamdani to be banned from the 25th-anniversary ceremony in September. Giovanni Galante, who lost his wife Grace, organized a petition citing Mamdani's public record and alleged minimization of 9/11 attacks.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is facing backlash after giving a ceremonial pen from a 9/11 remembrance ceremony to a top aide who once represented a convicted al Qaeda member whose brother-in-law hijacked the plane that struck the Pentagon.

Mamdani signed executive orders Friday ahead of the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 attacks, designating the date a citywide day of remembrance and service and strengthening efforts to prevent future terrorist threats.

After signing the final order, Mamdani handed the pen to NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch and asked her to pass it to chief counsel Ramzi Kassem. Kassem previously represented Ahmed al-Darbi, who pleaded guilty to war-crime charges tied to al Qaeda plots against commercial ships and was the brother-in-law of Khalid al-Mihdhar, one of the hijackers aboard American Airlines Flight 77, which crashed into the Pentagon, killing 184.
MAMDANI FACES GROWING 9/11 BACKLASH AS OLD POST RESURFACES AHEAD OF GROUND ZERO CEREMONY: 'IS THIS REAL?'
